paragraphs: In the morning, collect the service-area list and terminal. Walk streets and open cabinets to collect readings, cleaning dirty meters before photographing them. In the afternoon, flag and photograph an unusual reading at one home, inspect large commercial meters, and record water seepage in a control cabinet. Before leaving, synchronize the data and submit anomaly orders to the team leader.

In short, meter readers collect how much each customer used. They walk service areas, read dials, enter data in terminals, investigate anomalies, and report faults. They serve as the data-collection endpoint for billing through both walking and observation.
